general_information.Description: Aiming to develop practical teaching skills and pedagogical competencies, and to provide students with an overview of Japanese language teaching, this course introduces and provides practice in the following areas: 1. Basic elements of a Japanese language lesson. 2. Methods for designing and conducting Reading lessons (concepts, lesson design, materials, assessment, classroom activities). 3. Methods for designing and conducting Conversation lessons (concepts, lesson design, materials, assessment, classroom activities). 4. Methods for designing and conducting Writing lessons (concepts, lesson design, materials, assessment, classroom activities). 5. Methods for designing and conducting Listening lessons (concepts, lesson design, materials, assessment, classroom activities). 6. Active Learning teaching methods (concepts, characteristics, methods, assessment, and classroom activities).
general_information.StudentTasks: - Attend at least 80% of in-class hours to be eligible for the final exam. Students are responsible for fulfilling all requirements set by the instructor. - Actively participate in discussions and exchanges on topics and information presented in each lecture. - Gradually form teaching skills by identifying learner characteristics and preparing lesson content. - Prepare, practice, and conduct micro-teaching sessions according to language skills. - Review lectures, memorize new vocabulary, and keep a specialized vocabulary notebook to track and control learning progress. - Complete assigned tasks and exercises seriously and carefully.
general_information.Tools: 1) The instructor summarizes knowledge and experience of the course through lecture slides and provides exercises for students. 2) Relevant learning materials are linked to lectures via YouTube and websites. 3) Specialized Japanese-language textbooks are referenced (see Materials file).

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Apply practical pedagogical skills to real-world Japanese language teaching
Demonstrate proficient Japanese communication skills in both social and professional contexts, with the ability to identify and solve problems in the field of education
Understand and apply the distinctions between Reading, Listening, Speaking, and Writing lessons, integrating them effectively into pre-designed lesson plans

Enhance skills in working with learners, fostering group collaboration and creating an engaging classroom atmosphere. Develop situational handling and appropriate expression skills to respond clearly and effectively to learners’ questions related to lesson content
Implement Active Learning methods in classroom teaching

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Evaluation Criteria Attendance, attitude, classroom awareness, active participation in lectures Completion of assignments and tasks given by the instructor

・Students will be divided into groups to prepare and deliver demo lessons based on topics assigned by the instructor. ・Lesson content will be based on the Dekiru Nihongo curriculum, covering the four skills: Reading, Speaking, Writing, and Listening. ・Duration: Individual: 30 minutes per student (20 minutes of teaching content) Group: 45 minutes per group (30 minutes of teaching content) ・The instructor will evaluate and provide feedback in class.
Test 1: Knowledge related to teaching Reading, Listening, Speaking, and Writing lessons Test 2: Application of Active Learning methods in teaching practice

assessments.Note: 1) Final exams follow the official schedule set by the Examination Office. 2) To successfully complete the course, students must meet both of the following conditions: a) Process evaluation and midterm exam scores must be greater than 0; final exam score must be at least 4; the overall course score must be 5/10 or higher. b) No skill area in the final exam may receive a score of 0.

assessments.Question Type: Project in the form of a video + presentation
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Students will select a topic of their choice to record a 15- to 20-minute demo teaching video, incorporating Active Learning methods.
assessments.Note: The project topic must differ by at least 30% from the content used in the teaching practice assignment. Students must submit their project to the Examination Office on the final day of the course. Project grading consists of: Demo teaching video evaluation (50%) Presentation score (50%), including: 10-minute slide presentation of the project 10-minute Q&A session with the examiner
